evals.prompt: Idea: let users schedule the greeting to print at a set time every day. Plan it as a product and file the issues if I say yes.
evals.expected_output: Run in a copy of test/fixture-repo. Code-first questions, gated goal and approach, an approved roadmap on disk, and a host-neutral handoff.
expectations: The strategist read src/index.js or AGENTS.md before asking its first question
No question round asked more than 5 questions
Routine choices appear as a numbered Assumptions ledger, not as questions
Nothing was written to the repo: no docs/product/ folder, no commit offered
Drafts were written only under the solodev state folder's roadmaps/<slug>/, after the roadmap and work items were approved
The user approved a data model before the features were decomposed
roadmap.md has a Data model section with an erDiagram and each entity tagged with the feature that creates it
No feature exists only to build the schema; the first feature that needs an entity creates it
roadmap.md has Success criteria, Features as outcome-titled one-liners with Depends on, a Sequencing table, and an MVP line
Each items/F<n>.md has User story, Context, Proposed solution, Acceptance criteria, Out of scope, and Dependencies, risks and open questions sections
Each work item that touches data has a Data model section naming its entities and fields and linking the roadmap's Data model; items that touch no data have none
With no tracker available, the strategist said the drafts folder is the record and gave its path
When issues were filed, the epic was filed first with the roadmap as its body, and each feature's Data model section links it as #<epic>
Acceptance criteria are testable and use Given/When/Then where they describe behavior
Work item titles have the shape F<n>: <outcome-oriented title>
A fresh-context adversarial product-owner review of the drafted work items ran before the user was shown them
The work items shown to the user came with a review summary of findings applied and rejected
The handoff points each feature at /solodev-mission, one at a time, and prints `/solodev-mission #<n>` for wave 1's first feature when issues were filed
